# Backtest: run and optimize

<!-- Generated by scripts/core_docs.py; edit the source of truth and regenerate. -->

Use `Backtest` to run a `Strategy` subclass against one asset's historical data. Import both from `openbacktesting`. Start with the [complete first backtest](../quickstart.md) if you do not have a strategy yet.

[Backtest](#openbacktesting-backtest) · [DefaultOrderSize](#openbacktesting-defaultordersize)

## Run a strategy

```python
from openbacktesting import Backtest, Strategy
from openbacktesting.test import GOOG

class BuyAndHold(Strategy):
    def init(self):
        pass

    def next(self):
        if self.bar_index == 0:
            self.buy(qty=1)

bt = Backtest(GOOG, BuyAndHold, cash=10_000, commission=0.002,
              end_policy="close_at_last_close")
result = bt.run()
print(result[["Return [%]", "# Trades", "Max. Drawdown [%]"]])
print(result["_trades"])
```

`bt.run()` returns a pandas Series. Each call starts a new account and strategy instance. `commission=0.002` means **0.2% per execution**. The order placed on the first bar normally fills at the next bar's open. The end policy in this example closes remaining holdings at the final close.

## Constructor parameters

| Parameter | What to pass |
| --- | --- |
| `data` | pandas DataFrame with `Open`, `High`, `Low`, `Close`; `Volume` is optional unless an indicator needs it. See [data requirements](data.md). |
| `strategy` | Your `Strategy` subclass, without constructing an instance. |
| `cash` | Positive initial account balance; default 10,000. |
| `commission` | Fraction of execution notional, `(fixed_fee, fraction)`, a `Commission`, or a callable `(signed_qty, price) -> fee`. Charged on entries and exits. |
| `spread` | Fractional price adjustment on every execution; `0.001` means 0.1%. |
| `slippage` | `Slippage("bps", 5)` or `Slippage("fixed", 0.01)`; see [costs](trading.md#costs). |
| `margin` | Required margin as a fraction of notional, in `(0, 1]`; `1` is unleveraged. |
| `execution_timing` | `"next_open"` (default), or `"same_close"` for unconditional market orders submitted in `next()`. |
| `end_policy` | `"mark_to_market"` keeps final open holdings; `"close_at_last_close"` liquidates actual holdings and charges costs. |
| `instrument` | `InstrumentSpec` for quantity steps, minimum size, and optional price ticks. |
| `default_order_size` | `DefaultOrderSize("fixed", 1)` or `DefaultOrderSize("equity_fraction", 0.2)` used when `buy()`/`sell()` omit size. Default `None` requires explicit sizing. |
| `allow_short` | Whether new short positions may be opened; default `True`. |
| `max_gross_exposure` | Optional gross-notional/equity cap; valid exits remain allowed. |
| `hedging` | `False` nets opposite orders against existing trades; `True` allows long and short lots together. |
| `exclusive_orders` | A new ordinary entry cancels pending entries and submits exits for existing lots. Default `False`. |
| `context` | Optional `DataContext` for timeframe/timezone. Requires a timezone-aware index. |
| `risk_free_rate` | Annualized fraction used for statistics only; `0.03` means 3%. |
| `plotting`, `plotting_limits` | Collect visual declarations and optionally set resource limits. See [plotting](plotting.md). |
| `indicator_cache_bytes` | Retained indicator-cache budget; default 64 MiB, `0` disables reuse. Does not cap total process memory. |

`Backtest` uses the arguments you pass; it does not apply an `@backtest` decorator's settings. Use [runtime.run](runtime.md) when you want that declaration applied.

## Pass strategy parameters

Declare a class attribute (`length = 20`) or an [input](inputs.md), then call `bt.run(length=30)`. Keys are Python attribute names. For a title-based input request, use `inputs.request_for(MyStrategy, {"length": 30})` and `bt.run_inputs(request)`.

## Find a parameter combination

```python
from openbacktesting import Backtest, Strategy
from openbacktesting.test import GOOG

class MovingAverage(Strategy):
    length = 20

    def init(self):
        self.average = self.ta.sma(length=self.length)

    def next(self):
        if not self.average.valid[-1]:
            return
        if self.close[-1] > self.average[-1] and not self.position:
            self.buy(qty=1)
        elif self.close[-1] < self.average[-1] and self.position:
            self.position.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    bt = Backtest(GOOG, MovingAverage, end_policy="close_at_last_close")
    best, scores = bt.optimize(length=[10, 20, 40], maximize="Return [%]",
                               return_heatmap=True)
    print(best["_strategy"])
    print(scores)
```

Install the `optimize` extra before using optimization. Additional keyword arguments are candidate sequences for strategy parameters. `maximize` is a result key or a function receiving a result and returning a score; higher wins. `constraint=lambda p: p.fast < p.slow` filters combinations before running.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `method="grid"` | Evaluate the candidate product; input declarations support this method. |
| `method="sambo"` | Model-based search for ordinary class parameters; unavailable for declared inputs. |
| `max_tries` | Integer evaluation budget, or a fraction `(0, 1]` of the grid. Omit for an exhaustive grid; SAMBO defaults to 200. |
| `random_state` | Fixed integer for repeatable search sampling. |
| `return_heatmap=True` | Return `(best_result, scores)`; `scores` has a parameter MultiIndex. |
| `return_optimization=True` | SAMBO only: append the optimizer's raw result to the returned tuple. |

Use [saved experiments](optimizer.md) when you need complete reports for every candidate, filtering, or resume. `Backtest.optimize` returns the best run and optional scores.

## Read results and logs

`result["_equity_curve"]` contains the equity time series; `result["_trades"]` contains closed trade fragments. With the default end policy, open holdings appear in `result["_open_trades"]` and may contribute to return without contributing to `# Trades`. See [results](../guides/results.md) for units and tables, and [Portfolio](portfolio.md) for JSON reports.

Call `bt.get_logs()` after success or failure to read messages written through `self.log.info/warning/error`. A subsequent run clears the previous run's logs.

## Backtest

```python
Backtest(
    data,
    strategy,
    *,
    cash=10000,
    spread=0.0,
    commission=0.0,
    risk_free_rate=0.0,
    default_order_size=None,
    margin=1.0,
    execution_timing='next_open',
    instrument=None,
    slippage=None,
    allow_short=True,
    max_gross_exposure=None,
    hedging=False,
    exclusive_orders=False,
    end_policy='mark_to_market',
    indicator_cache_bytes=67108864,
    context=None,
    plotting=True,
    plotting_limits=None,
)
```

Store single-asset historical market data, strategy, and linear margin-account configuration.

<a id="openbacktesting-backtest-optimize"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Backtest.optimize -->

### Backtest.optimize

```python
Backtest.optimize(
    *,
    maximize='SQN',
    method='grid',
    max_tries=None,
    constraint=None,
    return_heatmap=False,
    return_optimization=False,
    random_state=None,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Search strategy-parameter combinations and select results by a specified statistic or scoring function.

<a id="openbacktesting-backtest-run"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Backtest.run -->

### Backtest.run

```python
Backtest.run(**kwargs)
```

Backtest strategy parameters and return a statistics Series, plain-value ledger tables, and an optional diagnostic strategy.

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Backtest.run_inputs -->

### Backtest.run_inputs

```python
Backtest.run_inputs(request)
```

Submit an input request with schemaVersion/schemaHash/values keyed by unique title.

### Backtest.get_logs

```python
Backtest.get_logs()
```

Return an independent copy of all strategy logs for this run; empty before any run.

## DefaultOrderSize

```python
DefaultOrderSize(mode, value)
```

Request budget when ordinary orders omit qty; does not represent a target position or filled notional.

| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="openbacktesting-defaultordersize-mode"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.DefaultOrderSize.mode -->`mode` | `str` | fixed asset quantity or equity_fraction. |
| <a id="openbacktesting-defaultordersize-value"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.DefaultOrderSize.value -->`value` | `float` | Positive quantity, or an equity fraction in (0, 1]. |

<a id="openbacktesting-defaultordersize-snapshot"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.DefaultOrderSize.snapshot -->

### DefaultOrderSize.snapshot

```python
DefaultOrderSize.snapshot()
```

Export independent mode and value.

<a id="openbacktesting-defaultordersize-from-snapshot"></a>

### DefaultOrderSize.from_snapshot

```python
DefaultOrderSize.from_snapshot(value)
```
